subsystems.name: Earth observation
subsystems.role: measures the conditions that drive shortages — rainfall, vegetation, soil moisture, crop area — from orbit.
parts: optical satellites (e.g. Sentinel-2 imagery, 10 m pixels)
radar satellites that see through cloud

subsystems.name: Ground telemetry
subsystems.role: tracks what is actually moving through warehouses, trucks and grids.
parts: GPS trackers on vehicles and shipments

subsystems.name: Data fusion layer
subsystems.role: turns messy, differently-formatted streams into one analysis-ready picture.

subsystems.name: Forecasting models
subsystems.role: predict where and when a shortage will appear, weeks to months ahead.

subsystems.name: Optimization engine
subsystems.role: converts predictions into a plan: what to send, from where, by which route.

subsystems.name: Alerting and decision layer
subsystems.role: puts the forecast in front of someone with the authority and budget to act.

buildSteps.title: Define the decision
buildSteps.detail: Start from a specific choice — how much grain to pre-position, where to send water trucks — and the lead time needed to make it useful.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Deploy sensors and trackers, and agree data-sharing terms with suppliers, utilities and agencies. Data rights are usually the hardest part.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the historical record
buildSteps.detail: Line up years of observations against logged shortage events so the model has something to learn from. Where records are thin, use surveys and field reports.

buildSteps.title: Train and validate the forecast
buildSteps.detail: Fit models on past seasons, then test them only on data they have never seen, and check performance region by region — a model that works nationally can fail in one district.

buildSteps.title: Quantify uncertainty
buildSteps.detail: Produce a probability, not a single number, so a 60% chance of a shortfall can be told apart from a 95% one.

buildSteps.title: Set trigger thresholds
buildSteps.detail: Agree in advance which forecast values release which pre-planned actions, so the response is not negotiated after the crisis starts.

buildSteps.title: Build the optimizer
buildSteps.detail: Encode warehouses, vehicle capacity, road conditions and budget as constraints, and solve for the allocation that best covers predicted need.

buildSteps.title: Run in shadow mode
buildSteps.detail: Operate the system alongside existing practice for a season, comparing its recommendations with what humans decided, before trusting it.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect outputs to procurement, pre-positioning and routing systems — with a human sign-off, because the cost of a false alarm is real money and the cost of a miss is lives.

prerequisites.why: public optical and radar imagery is what makes crop and rainfall monitoring affordable at continental scale.
supply chains are only forecastable if you can see stock and shipments in near real time.
it handles many noisy inputs and non-linear seasonal patterns better than fixed rules.
allocation across hundreds of depots and routes is a combinatorial problem no human can solve well.
the regions most at risk are usually the ones with the weakest reporting, so models train on the least data.

prerequisites.tech: Institutional readiness to act on a forecast
prerequisites.why: pre-arranged finance and authority are what turn a prediction into a delivery; without them the system only warns.

pathway.milestone: seasonal early-warning bulletins and food-security classifications inform appeals and planning
pathway.unlocks: weeks of extra lead time compared with reacting to visible crisis.

pathway.milestone: forecast-based financing: money released automatically when an agreed threshold is crossed
pathway.unlocks: action before a crisis peaks, which is far cheaper than response after it.

pathway.milestone: pre-positioning and dynamic routing driven by model output across whole regions
pathway.unlocks: stock placed where it will be needed rather than where it was last time.

pathway.milestone: integrated allocation across food, water, energy and health logistics
pathway.unlocks: one coherent plan instead of competing agency-by-agency supply chains — with the risk that a shared model becomes a single point of failure.
